Regional geology and hydrogeology were primarily sourced from U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) reports and scientific journals, which documented deep, medium, and shallow wells across the north and south coasts. Detailed data were sparse in local publications. The team assessed relevance in real time while reviewing references and excluded broader Caribbean studies unless they contained data specific to Puerto Rico. The researchers conducted technical visits to local universities and agencies in San Juan to gather additional information on local studies that contained rock and soil properties. 2.1.1 Regional Subsurface Review The island of Puerto Rico lies at the tectonically complex boundary between the Caribbean and North American plates, forming part of the Puerto Rico–Hispaniola microplate. The tectonic uplift associated with the subduction of the North American plate beneath the Caribbean plate exposed the island’s arc basement (Van Gestel et al. 1999). The northern margin of the island is bordered by the Puerto Rico Trench, which accommodates mainly left-lateral strike-slip motion with a component of subduction (Hayes et al. 1986), while the Muertos thrust belt to the south reflects compressional forces in the opposite direction (Van Gestel et al. 1999). Sedimentary sequences composed of carbonate and terrigenous deposits accumulated in the northern forearc basin from the Oligocene onward, following a long period of volcanic activity during the early Cretaceous to mid-Miocene (Hayes et al. 1986). These sequences dip gently northward due to regional Pliocene-Holocene tectonic tilting and tend to be thinner toward the eastern part of the basin, where the San Juan structural arch limits their thickness to less than 100 m in some areas (Renken et al. 2002). The tectonic evolution can be summarized as follows: Phase 1 Cretaceous-Eocene: formation and sedimentary infilling from a southern source. Phase 2 Oligocene-Pliocene: development of the Puerto Rico–Virgin Islands platform (~1,600 m thick), mainly carbonate rocks, thickening northward.
